speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; could you tell me when these symptoms first started and if they fluctuate in intensity?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of diplopia that worsens with looking up or down, and muscle weakness that fatigues with activity but improves with rest, is highly characteristic of this condition. I will request antibodies for acetylcholine receptor and MuSK as well as a single-fiber EMG to confirm.
